subject: Hosting fit & operational asks — ClearHealth post-call recap
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Casey <alex.casey@clearhealth.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Hosting fit & operational asks — ClearHealth post-call recap

Hi Alex — thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so we have alignment on hosting fit and isolation needs.

Call highlights (short):
- ClearHealth goal: embed clinical summarization + triage API into clinician workflow (low latency, PHI in transit).
- Key SLOs you called out: p99 generation latency target <200ms, availability target 99.9%, and strict US data residency (us-east preferred).
- Options on the table: Redwood Hosted API (shared), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem). You prioritized predictable latency and auditability over lowest unit cost.
- Top concerns: noisy-neighbor impact during spikes, isolation boundaries for PHI, and clear fallbacks if capacity is constrained.

Open questions we need from you to size a POC and recommendation:
1) Typical QPS (steady) and expected peak QPS (burst), and average token length per request.
2) Whether you need model weights on-prem or if managed-hosted with dedicated capacity is acceptable.
3) Any procurement timing / security questionnaire deadlines (SOC2 artifacts, network allowlist windows).

Our proposal / immediate next steps:
- Run a 2-week POC on Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) to validate latency and isolation. We suggest a minimal config to start: 2 reserved GPUs sized to your average QPS with autoscale headroom for bursts, plus prefix/KV caching enabled for warm sessions.
- We sent a draft SOW + SLA matrix (attached) that outlines scope, start/end, and success criteria.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Karthik to walk through connection patterns, IP allowlisting, and telemetry collection.

Please confirm the three items above and your preferred dates for the technical deep-dive (we have availability next week). If you prefer a Hosted API try first, we can run a dedicated-backed-hosted demo to show isolation/performance tradeoffs, but Dedicated gives the clearest isolation guarantees.

Attaching: redwood-poc-sow.pdf (draft), sla-matrix.xlsx, network-diagram.png (example topology).

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your procurement timeline.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
From: Alex Casey <alex.casey@clearhealth.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosting fit & operational asks — ClearHealth post-call recap

Thanks Mina — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock the POC:

1) Ballpark traffic: steady-state ~12 qps, peak bursts up to ~150 qps for 30–90s windows during shift changes. Typical payloads are 4–8k tokens.
2) We prefer to avoid on-prem model weights if possible. Dedicated/reserved in a US region is our ideal.
3) Procurement: we have a security review due in 3 weeks and procurement sign-off in ~6 weeks.

Two asks: can you include expected cost delta between Hosted (shared) with reserved capacity vs Dedicated (1 month committed) for the POC? Also, how do you guarantee that noisy neighbors won't impact p99 latency on the Hosted path — is there an SLA or shadowing/fallback?

Finally, please send the architecture diagram you referenced. If Dedicated meets the latency targets under our burst profile, we should be able to proceed to procurement.

— Alex
Alex Casey, CTO
ClearHealth
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Casey <alex.casey@clearhealth.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosting fit & operational asks — ClearHealth post-call recap

Alex — great, thanks for the traffic numbers, that gives us a concrete target. Short answers below and a few attachments/links.

Cost delta: initial estimate (very rough) for the 2-week POC:
- Hosted (shared) with reserved priority burst capacity: lower up-front cost but no strict compute isolation — estimated $3k–$5k for the window depending on tokens.
- Dedicated reserved pool (2 GPU equivalent) for 2 weeks: higher committed cost but predictable latency — estimated $18k–$25k depending on instance class.

Noisy-neighbor guarantees / fallback:
- Hosted shared path: we provide priority routing and soft-reservation but cannot guarantee p99 under extreme cluster contention; we recommend only if you can tolerate sporadic p99 spikes and want lower cost.
- Dedicated: physical/reserved pool eliminates cross-tenant compute interference; combined with prefix/KV cache and per-tenant request queuing we can meet your p99 target in our tests. We'll include a runbook for graceful fallback to a smaller model variant if the pool reaches saturation.

Architecture diagram and docs: attached network-diagram.png and this doc that explains Dedicated vs Hosted internals: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bz-clearhealth-poc (see README).

Next step: Karthik suggested a technical deep-dive to nail down ingress patterns and telemetry. Can you do Tue 11/08 or Wed 11/09 at 10am PT? If that works we'll send calendar invites and the draft SOW via DocuSign for signature so procurement can start review.

Let me know and we'll lock schedules.

— Mina
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Technical constraints & POC config suggestions (ClearHealth)

Internal note — copying the POC recommendations I plan to bring to the deep-dive: please keep this internal until we align on exact sizing.

POC objectives: validate p99 <200ms across 150 qps bursts with typical 4–8k token payloads and PHI transit. Validate logging / audit retention.

Suggested POC config:
- Dedicated reserved pool: start with 2x A100-class instances (or equivalent 80GB memory) with option to add a third for burst headroom. If cost constrained, T4s with aggressive quantization might work but risk higher p99.
- Runtime config: persistent KV cache per-tenant, warm-start prefetch for expected prompt prefixes, and continuous batching tuned to keep per-request latency under budget.
- Networking: require egress/ingress IP allowlist; we'll provide NAT IPs for the Dedicated pool. Need ClearHealth to provide their allowlist CIDRs plus any VPN details.
- Telemetry: require RT metrics (p50/p95/p99, token throughput), request/response sampling (1%), and access to audit logs for the POC window.

Items I need from ClearHealth before the call:
1) Exact allowlist CIDR(s) and whether they use a proxy that will change source IPs.
2) The JWT/OAuth flow specifics they plan to use (token lifetimes, rotation).
3) Confirmation they can accept our sample telemetry endpoint and retention window (14 days by default for POC).

I'll bring a runbook showing failure modes and the planned automatic fallback to a smaller model (or queueing policy) if saturation occurs.

— Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood
